//: SCOPING IS THE POINT OF THIS FILE. The project hosts more than one application. Both blocks below name their target explicitly so a deploy from this repo cannot reach anything that is not ours. Never run a bare 'firebase deploy'.

hosting.//: site, not target: this pins the deploy to teachercorner-dev.web.app. Without it a hosting deploy would go to the project default site, which is someone else's.

rewrites.//: SPA fallback, so a hard refresh on /dashboard resolves instead of 404ing.

headers.//: ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. Everything revalidates by default, and the hashed assets below opt back out. Where two rules match one file, the LATER one wins.
headers.//why: The previous rule named '/index.html', which never matched: the SPA rewrite serves index.html for '/' and for every deep route, so the request path is '/dashboard' or '/', never '/index.html'. Every visitor therefore got Firebase's default hour on the one file that must not be cached, and kept booting an old bundle for an hour after each deploy.

headers.//: Angular hashes these filenames, so a changed file gets a new name and can never be served stale. Listed AFTER the catch-all so it overrides it.

functions.//: ONLY this directory is declared. ../functions holds an unwired email-code flow with no package.json; declaring it would sweep requestLoginCode/verifyLoginCode into the deploy and demand SMTP secrets. Add a second entry here when that flow is wanted.
functions.//codebase: A NAMED codebase, and it is load-bearing. helix-staging-india already runs sendWelcomeEmail and expenseLogTotals, neither of which carries a codebase label, so both sit in the DEFAULT codebase. Deploying into 'default' from here would make the CLI see those two as present-in-my-codebase-but-absent-from-my-source and offer to DELETE them. The CLI only ever considers same-codebase functions for deletion, so a name of our own puts other teams' functions structurally out of reach.

firestore.//: SAFE NOW, and it was not before. This app owns 'teacher-corner-dev' outright, so a rules deploy from this repo cannot reach any other database. The database id is load-bearing: omitting it targets the default database, where other apps live.
